first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this with 'look at the garden one, Mum'. It's nicely written, plain English, no silly slang, and it reads like a proper etiquette guide rather than an Instagram caption. I read it top to bottom on the iPad. Most of it is for her, not me: forks on the left, napkin folds, which glass goes where. I perked up at the destination section, where it says to ask the venue questions early and get the answers in writing. That's the bit I'd forward to Geoff. What it doesn't touch is the money side of hiring things in, and nothing about whether Mum can actually get to the table.

journey.quote: For a wedding abroad, it also sets out what to ask the venue before you fall for a look its cupboards cannot deliver.
journey.reaction: Good. Sensible before pretty. That's the sort of warning I want her to hear from someone other than me.

journey.section: The place setting, piece by piece
journey.quote: Treat them as a well-tested framework rather than a set of Australian rules, and adapt them to your menu.
journey.reaction: I like that they say where the rules come from and don't make anyone feel silly for not knowing them. Honest.

journey.quote: The most useful rule for a wedding is the simplest: only set the cutlery your guests will use.
journey.reaction: Quite right, and it's the kind of thing that saves money on hire as well, though they don't say so.

journey.quote: Below, each theme is translated into the same five choices: plate, cutlery finish, glass, napkin and stationery.
journey.reaction: Seven themes of bullet points. Easy to read on the iPad, but this part is really for my daughter. I skimmed until the destination section.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Ask these questions early, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: Yes. In writing. That's the line I'd underline for Geoff.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Which pieces would need to be hired in for our theme and guest count?
journey.reaction: And then what? Who books the hire, who pays the deposit on it, and who's responsible if half the glasses turn up broken in Italy? The page stops just where my questions start.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the setting you approve is the setting your guests sit down to.
journey.reaction: That's reassuring. Someone accountable, and it's on paper before we pay.

journey.section: What to check at the trial table
journey.quote: Sightlines. Sit down. Can you see and speak to the guest opposite?
journey.reaction: Thank you. The older relatives can't hear across a forest of flowers. Practical.

journey.section: What to check at the trial table
journey.quote: Spacing between places. Ask the venue or stylist what each guest needs for your chosen setting and chairs, and confirm it against your guest count.
journey.reaction: My mother uses a walking frame. Is there room to get her in and out of her chair at a long table on a terrace? This is the obvious spot to say so, and it doesn't.

journey.quote: To keep the seating plan and name cards in one place, [plan seating and name cards in Wonderland Studio](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-studio).
journey.reaction: What is Wonderland Studio? Is it free, or another thing to pay for? I wouldn't click it without knowing.

journey.section: Set the table with someone in your corner
journey.quote: With one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, the questions to the venue, the mock-up and the final setting sit with one person who knows your plans.
journey.reaction: One person. Good. I'd want their name and a phone call before anything's booked.

unanswered_questions: If pieces have to be hired in abroad, who books and pays for the hire, and who is responsible if items are broken or missing on the day? (deferred business detail: sourcing and hire)
Are hire deposits held in AUD or euros, and are they protected? (deferred business detail: fees and payments)
How is the Wedded Concierge fee charged, and do you take a commission on hire or styling? (deferred business detail)
Is there room at a long banquet table for a guest with a walking frame or wheelchair, and should we ask the venue about step-free access to the reception area?
What is Wonderland Studio, and does it cost anything?
Is the first step a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as the parent paying part?
Who do we ring on the day if the tables aren't set the way we approved?

turn_offs_found.quote: Which pieces would need to be hired in for our theme and guest count?
turn_offs_found.why: My card says no mention of contracts, deposits or who is responsible is a turn-off. The page raises hiring things in overseas but never says who carries the risk. I understand the business may not want to say yet, but it's what I'd look for.

would_share_with: My husband, the destination section from 'ask for the answers in writing' through 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit'
My daughter, the whole thing, especially 'only set the cutlery your guests will use' so she doesn't overspend on hire

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like that handled for you, our [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=22-amazing-table-settings-for-every-wedding-theme&utm_content=primary) team can take the venue questions from here.
cta_reaction.why: It's the right offer for me: someone else chasing the venue, in writing. But a table settings article isn't where I'd decide to hand over money. I'd click to see who they are, then ring before anything is booked. It would help if the page said the first step is a conversation, but I won't hold it against them if that's not confirmed.

top_3_changes: Add mobility to the trial-table spacing check (a question, no measurement). Old: "- **Spacing between places.** Ask the venue or stylist what each guest needs for your chosen setting and chairs, and confirm it against your guest count." New: "- **Spacing between places.** Ask the venue or stylist what each guest needs for your chosen setting and chairs, and confirm it against your guest count, including room for any guest who uses a walking frame or wheelchair."

Add one access question to the destination checklist. Old: "- Who sets the tables, and who clears them between courses?" New: "- Who sets the tables, and who clears them between courses?\n- Can guests with limited mobility reach the reception tables without steps?"

Carry 'in writing' into the destination FAQ so it matches the body. Old: "then see the pieces laid at a mock-up before you commit." New: "then get the answers in writing and see the pieces laid at a mock-up before you commit."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on who is responsible, writing, elderly guests and a phone call
No invented brand facts; hire responsibility, deposits, fees, commissions, Wonderland Studio cost and on-the-day contact placed in unanswered_questions
Suggested edits stay within limits: no fees, commissions, sourcing, vetting or hire claims, no new facts or measurements, exact old/new strings
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Hire responsibility, deposits and fees are deferred business details; flag for the business rather than fill. Should the panel note it as a known gap for the funding parent?

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad. Relevance is 2 because a styling and etiquette guide is written for the couple; only the destination and trial-table sections speak to her.

Likelihood to enquire is 2 because of topic fit, not distrust: trust is 4 thanks to 'in writing' and one Wedded Advisor. Deferred business details (hire, deposits, fees) are not penalised as must-fix.
Husband's name (Geoff) and the walking frame are character colour from the persona card and earlier panels, not page facts.
Fast mode: full article read; theme lists and FAQ skimmed as she would.
